pong-cabinet.title: Pong — production cabinet
pong-cabinet.source: Wikimedia Commons — Atari Pong arcade game cabinet
pong-cabinet.sourceCredit: Photograph by Rob Boudon; crop and retouching by Ubcule.
pong-cabinet.displayCredit: Photo © Rob Boudon · adapted by Ubcule · CC BY 2.0
pong-cabinet.basis: The photograph is offered under CC BY 2.0 with credit, a license link and modifications identified. The depicted cabinet and marks are reproduced for contextual criticism and identification.
pong-cabinet.purpose: Show the production cabinet, shared display and minimal controls that made a paid match an immediately approachable social activity.
pong-cabinet.treatment: Source derivative retained in full, including its existing crop and retouching. Our changes: proportional resizing, WebP compression and metadata removal. No recoloring, added branding or content retouching.

pong-doubles-social-1973.title: Pong Doubles — German promotional photograph, 1973
pong-doubles-social-1973.source: International Arcade Museum — Pong Doubles German brochure, inside page 2
pong-doubles-social-1973.sourceCredit: Archive contributors: Steffen and Laschek. Photographer not identified in the brochure or record.
pong-doubles-social-1973.purpose: Examine the tennis clothing and rackets used to make a new electronic pastime recognizable as social recreation. This is staged advertising, not a documentary photograph of tavern customers.
pong-doubles-social-1973.provenanceNote: Pong Doubles is the four-player follow-up, not the 1972 prototype or the original two-player cabinet. The adjacent inside page discusses partners, rematches and public venues; those are sales claims, not measured player behavior.
pong-doubles-social-1973.basis: Contextual criticism and review of the pictured design and commercial offer. This records the editorial rationale, not bespoke permission from the publisher or archive.
pong-doubles-social-1973.treatment: Full source image and visible notices retained; proportionally resized and compressed to responsive WebP. No AI reconstruction, added marks or cropping of the source.

gauntlet-gameplay-1985.title: Gauntlet — arcade gameplay
gauntlet-gameplay-1985.sourceCredit: Game credited to Ed Logg, Bob Flanagan and the Atari Games team. Capture author not named by the archive.
gauntlet-gameplay-1985.purpose: Inspect distinct score/health readouts, empty character slots inviting entry, and a visible one-coin-to-700-health exchange. The number is this capture’s configured allowance, not a universal default.
gauntlet-gameplay-1985.treatment: Complete native 336 × 240 frame, lossless WebP. CSS preserves the pixel grid. Optional labeled outlines sit above the image; the source file is unchanged and can be inspected without overlays.
gauntlet-gameplay-1985.basis: Contextual criticism and review of the pictured design and commercial offer. This records the editorial rationale, not bespoke permission from the publisher or archive.

atari-vcs-sales-1977.title: Atari VCS — 1977 sales catalog, inside front page
atari-vcs-sales-1977.source: Atarimania — Atari 1977 US sales catalog, page 2 of 12
atari-vcs-sales-1977.sourceCredit: Atari sales literature, preserved by Atarimania. Individual photographer and scan contributor are not named in the catalog record.
atari-vcs-sales-1977.purpose: Examine how Atari pitched the reusable home machine to retailers: its cartridge library and continuing software sales were part of the hardware offer. The staged console/TV photograph supplies the historical product context.
atari-vcs-sales-1977.provenanceNote: A period trade sales page, not a photograph of a household or a current product advertisement. Its future cartridge schedule and claims of superiority are promotional statements, not measured results.

combat-box-1977.title: Combat — original 1977 package front
combat-box-1977.sourceCredit: Cover illustration: Cliff Spohn (also credited in MobyGames, https://www.mobygames.com/game/8851/combat/). Game: Larry Wagner and Joe Decuir with Atari’s development team. Scan contributor not individually named by the archive.
combat-box-1977.displayCredit: © Atari · cover art: Cliff Spohn · Atarimuseum.de
combat-box-1977.purpose: Identify the game included with the VCS at launch and examine its promise of variety: the package sells 27 game variations within one cartridge, making the initial hardware purchase immediately playable.
combat-box-1977.provenanceNote: The archive identifies this as 1977 packaging. Combat’s inclusion with the launch console and 27 variations are independently documented by the Science Museum Group (object 2007-5026/5). Space Invaders was a later 1980 release, not the 1977 pack-in.
